sections.h2: Why is Union County called the Top of Georgia?
sections.html:
Brasstown Bald, the highest mountain in Georgia, rises in the southeast corner of Union County and straddles the Towns County line. That is why locals call the county the Top of Georgia. The county measures 329.02 square miles, with 322.55 of them land, and Blairsville is the seat.

Union was carved from Cherokee County territory in the Georgia Land Lottery of 1832, after gold found in the 1820s made land long held by Native Americans more attractive to settlers. The county history page says the name probably traces to the Union Party, not to the Civil War, which came nearly thirty years later. Residents live in Blairsville, in the community of Suches, or out in the countryside among pastures and creeks.

For a seller, that mix means very different parcels: a mountain cabin with a view, a lot in town, or acreage with road frontage. Each needs its own approach to pricing, access and, above all, a clean tax record before closing.

sections.h2: What is daily life like in Union County?
sections.html:
The county describes itself as an easy drive of about 90 miles from Atlanta, with rolling pastures, mountain views, clear creeks and waterfalls. Its pages note that Blairsville was named among the Top Ten Places for Retirement in a 1994 Wall Street Journal article and in a 2008 Retire in Georgia feature, and they point to a local hospital and public school system as selling points.

The county's own summary cites about 54 people per square mile from the 2020 count of 24,632. Acreage, mountain parcels and in-town lots are all assessed under the same 40% rule, so the bill depends mostly on land size, exemptions and any current-use covenant that comes with the parcel. Check which of those apply before you price.

sections.h2: What do the numbers show for Union County homes?
sections.html:
Mid-2025 estimates give Union County 27,859 people, a 13.1% jump from the 24,632 counted in 2020. Owners live in 84.4% of housing units, and the middle owner-occupied value is $307,400, the highest figure among the counties in this area of Georgia.

Seniors make up 36.8% of the population, and households average 2.24 people. The county's own pages describe Blairsville as a retirement destination, and 264 building permits in 2025 point to steady construction. Estates of older owners are a likely source of listings.

sections.h2: Which Union County office do I call?
sections.html:
Billing and valuing sit in different offices. The tax commissioner's site says its mission is to bill, collect and disburse taxes, while the assessors alone determine value.

  • Tax commissioner: (706) 439-6017, at the courthouse, 65 Courthouse Street in Blairsville, for bills, payments and tag and title work.
  • Tax assessors: (706) 439-6011, open weekdays until half past four, for values, returns, homestead filings and exemptions.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds, including a copy of your warranty deed.

Seven staff keep the parcel records: five real-property appraisers, one personal property appraiser and a clerk. A posted public notice says the county hired Georgia Mass Appraisal Solutions and Services to help revalue residential, commercial, industrial and farm parcels. Field crews drive vehicles with a Union County seal and stay outside homes and buildings.

sections.h2: What is the Union County property tax due date, and what do late bills cost?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner's FAQ puts the real estate and business personal property deadline at December 20 annually. Mobile and modular homes are due April 1, vehicles follow the owner's birthday, and boats share the December 20 date after May assessment notices.

After the deadline, 1% interest accrues every month on the balance. Past 90 days, the office can record a tax lien, called a FIFA, at the Clerk of Superior Court, and it warns that credit bureaus can read those public records. Tax sale proceedings may start at the same 90-day mark.

  • The county allows at least 60 days to pay the annual bill.
  • A bill that never arrived still has to be paid.
  • Blairsville issues and collects its own city property tax.

Land sellers should also know that standing timber is not taxed until it is sold or harvested, and then at 100% of fair market value. A lump-sum timber sale needs the buyer to send the tax and form PT-283T to the tax commissioner within five business days of purchase.

sections.h2: How does a Union County appeal work?
sections.html:
Notices of value go out in May, and the challenge period runs 45 days after the notice date. The first filing goes to the Board of Assessors. If no agreement follows, the file is forwarded to the Board of Equalization, which the Grand Jury appoints, and a further written notice to the assessors takes the case to Superior Court.

Arbitration or a certified hearing officer can replace the board for some owners, and that choice is made at filing. Mobile and modular home owners can contest twice, once at the return stage and again within 45 days after the bill goes out, which the county says is usually mid February.

Skipping a required return can draw a 10% penalty on the value not returned, plus interest. Real estate returns are expected from January 1 to April 1 for property that changed hands or changed in value.

sections.h2: How does homestead relief work in Union County?
sections.html:
Take a copy of your warranty deed to the assessors and apply before April 1. The house must be yours and be where you live on January 1. Once approved, relief continues until you move, and a late application starts the following year.

The tax commissioner's site says Union's local homestead exemptions beat the state's, while the state revenue department's county page lists none, so ask the assessors for current figures before relying on either. Freeport covers business inventory, and current-use programs for farm and forest land demand a commitment to stay undeveloped, with stiff penalties for breaking it.

sections.h2: What should I do about the tax bill when I sell in Union County?
sections.html:
County bills are mailed to whoever held the property on January 1, so a buyer closing in March or September will not receive that year's statement. Arrange for the closing agent to pay it from your proceeds and request a written payoff from the tax office.

The tax commissioner confirms that a new owner gets no bill for the purchase year, so check any prorated payment on the settlement statement closely. For a mountain rental or a cabin left by a relative, ask about each year it was held. A cash sale can finish the payoff and the deed recording in a single courthouse visit.

faqs.q: When must Union County property tax be paid?
faqs.a: By December 20 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile and modular homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: What does a late Union County payment cost?
faqs.a: The tax site states 1% interest a month. A lien can follow once 90 days pass.

faqs.q: How long can I appeal a Union County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after the notice date. The Board of Assessors hears it first, then the Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: Can I file a Union County homestead application late?
faqs.a: A late filing does not help the current year, but the assessors activate it for the next one.

faqs.q: Who collects Blairsville city property tax?
faqs.a: Blairsville bills its own portion. The county tax commissioner handles county and school bills.
